title: The 'for each' idea
idea: A loop lets you say 'for each thing, do this one step.' Meet the idea and see the repeated output it produces. Stays at the plain-English loop level.

exercises.prompt: A loop is a way to tell the computer to...
options: Do the same step again for each thing, without copying it
exercises.explanation: A loop repeats one step for each thing in a group. That's the 'for each' idea at the heart of this lap.

exercises.prompt: 'For each' means: run the same body once per item.
exercises.explanation: Exactly. One item, one run of the body; next item, body again. That repeats until the items run out.

exercises.prompt: If you loop 'for each of 3 guests: print Welcome', what shows on the screen?
exercises.explanation: The body 'print Welcome' runs once per guest — three guests, three Welcome lines. That's visible, predictable output.

exercises.prompt: Looping 'for each of 4 items: print Hi' prints how many lines?
exercises.explanation: One Hi per item, four items — four lines. Output lines match the number of things with a single-print body.

exercises.prompt: A loop saves you from copying the same print line over and over.
exercises.explanation: You write the body once; the loop repeats it. That's the fix for the copy-paste pain from Unit 35.

exercises.prompt: Which everyday sentence matches the 'for each' idea best?
options: If the plate is dirty, wash it
exercises.explanation: 'For each plate, wash it' is a loop in plain English: one body (wash it), repeated per plate.

exercises.prompt: Match each 'for each' loop to its number of output lines (body is a single print).

pairs.left: For each of 2 things: print Go
For each of 5 things: print Go
For each of 1 thing: print Go

exercises.explanation: With one print in the body, lines equal the number of things looped over.

exercises.prompt: In 'for each of 3 things: print Hi', which part is the BODY?
exercises.explanation: The body is the indented step that repeats: print Hi. The 'for each' part controls how many times it runs.

exercises.prompt: A loop with 0 things to go through runs its body 0 times.
exercises.explanation: No things means the body never runs — nothing prints. Loops handle 'none' gracefully.

exercises.prompt: Why is the 'for each' idea such a big deal?
options: It turns 'do this many times' into one short, clear instruction
exercises.explanation: One readable loop can stand for hundreds of repeats. You just met the core tool of this whole lap.
